articles.title: Pat Cummins to remain Test captain after Cricket Australia board expresses ‘unanimous’ support
articles.summary: Bowler to keep leadership role amid sandpapergate saga. Josh Hazlewood also throws support behind embattled captain. Cricket Australia has thrown its “unanimous” support behind embattled Test captain Pat Cummins, saying the bowler will continue in his leadership role despite the intense pressure on…
body: Cummins’s position as captain had been called into question after the publication of Usman Khawaja’s memoir, in which the former Australia opener claimed the entire team knew of the plot to tamper with the ball on the tour of South Africa in 2018.
But after the CA chair, David Boon, and the CEO, Todd Greenberg, met with Cummins in Sydney on Friday, they gave him their full backing in a statement on Saturday.

“We’ve expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa,” Boon said. “We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat’s integrity has been compromised.”
Cummins will keep the captaincy ahead of the summer Test series against New Zealand on home soil, with a tour to India to follow early next year.

articles.title: Bayern Munich confirm Harry Kane ‘out for next few months’ with ankle injury
articles.summary: England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne. Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’ Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.
body: Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.

A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”

The Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Said El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.

articles.title: No late drama needed: Talon Immel and a stifling defense send Burnt Hills to the state semifinals
articles.summary: COLONIE-Coming off a nail-biting win in last week's Section 2 Class A championship, the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team hoped to avoid more late-game drama in Friday's state quarterfinal against Section 9 Cornwall.
body: The game stayed tight for much of the first half, but Burnt Hills used its explosive run game and a big defensive effort to punch a ticket to the state semifinals with a 31-14 win at Colonie High School.

"We feel great," Burnt Hills junior running back Talon Immel said. "We know we have tough tasks ahead and it's not done yet. We're going to keep grinding throughout this week at practice and we're going to give everything we got and hopefully it falls our way."

"I'm so proud of them," Spartans coach Kevin DeBonis said. "The belief in each other has grown each week and each day, really. The life lessons we talk about, they're seeing more and more how they come to pass and they're applying them. You want to teach them about life. It's great to win, but when you have so many unselfish guys out here pushing in the same direction, it's really cool."

Three different Spartans recorded touchdown runs on Friday, including Immel, who found the end zone twice. Junior quarterback Tristan West recorded a 4-yard touchdown to start the scoring with 4:35 left in the first quarter and junior running back Owen Huggins put a cap on his team's scoring with a 2-yard run midway through the fourth quarter.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody
articles.summary: Comedian Stavros Halkias voices fictional shock jock. Segment echoes Watson, Tucker misconduct allegations. Rockstar’s latest skewers American sports culture. The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses…
body: The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players.

Halkias, voicing outspoken sports talk radio host Dominick “The Brick” Brizzolato in a withering caricature of right-wing media bombast, argues the player was not responsible for becoming sexually aroused during a massage and instead blames the therapist, in an apparent parody of the defenses offered on behalf of athletes accused of sexual misconduct.

“Be the voice of reason here,” Halkias begins. “You know, there is extreme idiocy and stupidity on both sides, folks. I mean, think. Put yourself in Ross’s shoes. OK, you’re a pro football player, a warrior in a proud tribe called the Vice City Manatees. You’re getting treated by the team masseuse after a rough game, after leaving it all out on the field. You’re on the table and your penis gets hard, allegedly.

articles.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
articles.summary: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one. In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture.
body: order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance.

In the echo of all of this, many media members covering the match in the press box received an email from DC United, the local Major League Soccer club that operates and rents out Audi Field to the Spirit. It was a press release announcing the dismissal of their head coach, René Weiler. As the Spirit celebrated a third consecutive championship appearance on the pitch below, some unfortunate soul in a nearby office was tasked with sending that notice, the final nail in yet another dreadful season. While the women have thrived, the local men’s team has not made the playoffs in nearly a decade.

articles.title: Anthony Muñoz opens putt-putt course at The Banks with hole-in-one
articles.summary: Pro Football Hall of Famer and former Cincinnati Bengals great Anthony Muñoz opened the new putt-putt golf course at The Banks with a hole-in-one. The Banks' Twitter/X account shared video of the hole-in-one on Muñoz's ceremonial first putt. It was reminiscent of a 2019 putt by Donzetta Nuxhall.
body: Muñoz was asked on Fox 19 before a 2024 Bengals' preseason game against Tampa Bay whether he thought rookie Amarius Mims, the Bengals' first-round draft pick earlier that year, was ready to emerge as the team's starter at right tackle.

"From what I've seen, I've been to three practices. I would be 100 percent comfortable having No. 71 at the right tackle protecting Joe Burrow," Muñoz said. "What I've seen has been amazing for a man that big. The way he moves, the way he's able to dip. But the most important thing that I've noticed for a rookie offensive lineman is the patience he has in pass pro."

articles.title: Jackets fall 88-82 in COFH – Men’s Basketall Edition
articles.summary: In his first Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate basketball game as Tech’s head coach, Scott Cross’ Jackets fell 88-82 to the Georgia Bulldogs in front of 8,600 fans. The loss is Tech’s first of the season, falling to 5-1. The Bulldogs climb to 6-0.
body: The differentiator ended up being the very beginning of the game. Tech’s Victor Valdes committed two early fouls and was taken out early while Georgia went up 10-0. Tech went down as much as 19 near the end of the first half. Georgia also outrebounded the Jackets 41-30, including 14-6 on the offensive end.
Colby Garland and Tylis Jordan both led Tech in points with 19 apiece, Garland playing almost 31 minutes off the bench. Georgia’s Kanon Catchings also finished with 19 points.
Kayden Allen came through in a big way off the bench with 16 points, 12 coming the second half on 5-9 shooting.
Afer battling injury, Cole Kirouac played seven minutes off the bench with two assists and thre rebounds.

articles.title: Cost of Man Utd hiring and firing managers nears £100m
articles.summary: Manchester United borrowed £10m three days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino would be their new head coach, which will cost them £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer.
body: Manchester United borrowed another £10m three days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.

In an extended Stock Market filing to go with their first-quarter financial results that were released on Thursday, United said they would be liable to pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer to hire the Argentine.
United announced Pochettino had agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal on 13 November. They borrowed £10m on 16 November.
The loan is one of three confirmed after the 30 September first-quarter reporting date, which takes the overall amount owed on their rolling credit limit to £240m.

articles.title: Kentucky Basketball continues to make the wrong kind of history under Mark Pope
articles.summary: Kentucky Basketball head coach Mark Pope continues to make history for the wrong reasons. The Wildcats fell to Indiana, 90-76, on Friday night inside Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana.
body: In addition, Kentucky is all the way down to 64th overall at KenPom. That’s the Wildcats’ lowest ranking since the 2007-08 season (78) and the second-lowest in the KenPom era, which dates back to the 1996-97 season.

The ‘07-08 team was led by Billy Gillispie, one of the most unsuccessful head coaches in Kentucky Basketball history. Being compared to one of the program’s worst coaches is never a good sign for Pope.
While Friday night’s loss was not by 19 points, losing by 14 after holding a 47-45 halftime lead was still incredibly disappointing.
For Pope, the schedule does not get any easier. Kentucky will face Wichita State, Virginia, Louisville, and North Carolina before SEC play begins.

articles.title: Kim moves clear at LPGA finale after hole-in-one
articles.summary: South Korea's A-Lim Kim aces the par-three 16th on her way to claiming a three-shot lead after the second round of CME Group Tour Championship.
body: The 31-year-old held a share of the lead after the first round at Tiburon Golf Club in Florida but is out on her own after shooting a superb 64 on Friday.
Kim made seven birdies and one eagle, the hole-in-one on 16, with a solitary bogey to head into the weekend 15 under and with a great chance of claiming the $4m (£3.05m) top prize.
"When I hit, after, I felt it was a little strong, but hit the pin and then went in," Kim said of her hole-in-one, the third of her career. "I think it was luck."
On the potential to win millions on Sunday, she added: "Money is money. It has not bothered me. I think winning is more important for me."

articles.title: First defeat and first red for Ferguson as Glens falter
articles.summary: BBC Sport Northern Ireland looks at Duncan Ferguson's first red card and defeat as Glentoran manager as they are edged out 3-2 by Cliftonville on Friday.
body: It was a night of unfortunate firsts for Duncan Ferguson at Solitude on Friday.
The Everton great suffered his first defeat as Glentoran boss as they were edged out 3-2 by Cliftonville in an Irish Premiership thriller.

He also received his first red card as a manager, after picking up nine during his playing career, in the first half for protesting the decision to award Cliftonville's first goal after he perceived a foul in the build-up.
The defeat ended Glentoran's eight-game unbeaten run in the league and leaves them well off the pace in pursuit of their first league title since 2009.

articles.title: Kim leads LPGA Tour finale after amazing ace as Hull and Korda chase
articles.summary: A Lim Kim fired a hole-in-one on her way to grabbing the halfway lead at the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship, where Charley Hull remains in contention.
body: Kim holed her tee shot with a seven iron at the 168-yard par-three 16th, with the Korean adding seven birdies and a lone bogey in a round-of-the-day 64 at Tiburon Golf Club.

The former US Women's Open champion was tied at the top of the leaderboard until her stunning ace and a birdie at the par-five next, which moved Kim to 15 under and three clear of back-to-back defending champion Jeeno Thitikul.

Thitikul posted five birdies in a seven-hole stretch on her back nine during a second-round 67, putting her in the final group on Saturday, with Hull a further shot back in a share of third after matching the world No 2's score.

Yuri Yoshida, Ina Yoon, Yan Liu, Jenny Bae and Auston Kim complete the logjam on 11 under alongside Hull, who posted five birdies in a blemish-free round as the 2016 champion looks to win the CME Group Tour Championship for a second time.

articles.title: Price survives match darts to reach Grand Slam semis
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price faces two match darts before winning a thrilling quarter-final against Nico Springer at the Grand Slam of Darts, as Luke Littler's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena is knocked out.
body: Gerwyn Price faced two match darts before winning a thrilling quarter-final against Nico Springer at the Grand Slam of Darts, as Luke Littler's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena was knocked out.
Three-time champion Price led for most of the match but his German opponent refused to let him out of reach.
Springer missed a number of chances to level, including three darts at double top to make it 13-13 as he fell 14-12 behind, before he eventually made it 14-14 and then took a 15-14 lead.
However, Price produced a stunning 143 checkout to take it to a decider in which Springer had the throw.

articles.title: Kane set to miss three months with ankle injury
articles.summary: Harry Kane is expected to be sidelined for three months after suffering an ankle injury during Bayern Munich's Bundesliga game with Cologne on Friday.
body: Sky Germany report Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed shortly after the 1-1 draw that Kane had suffered a "syndesmosis ligament tear" - also known as a high ankle sprain.
The Ballon d'Or winner - who became England's most-capped player last week - was seeking a first goal in five matches for the Bundesliga leaders.

However, as he looked to latch on to Michael Olise's deflected low cross at the back post, Cologne full-back Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow through.
Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

articles.title: Hazlewood backs Cummins to remain as Test captain after sandpaper 'pile-on'
articles.summary: Josh Hazlewood has defended Pat Cummins over a “pile-on” around Sandpapergate and refused to rule out boycotting the Test team if he is made to step down as captain.
body: Hazlewood became the latest player to break their silence over his involvement in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, which has dominated headlines again since comments from Australian team-mate Usman Khawaja in his new autobiography 'Sabr' claimed the whole team were aware of using sandpaper.

Cameron Bancroft plunged Australian cricket into further turmoil with a 4,000-word statement, backing claims "the whole team" knew about the plot and contradicting strong denials Cummins offered in his press conference a few days earlier.

Cummins had branded Khawaja's testimony "complete and utter nonsense" and "100 per cent wrong", leading Bancroft to go public with his story, while Australia's Test captain has had his future speculated after how he has handled the incident.

"It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days [at Cummins] from different people," Hazlewood told CodeSports. "I want to back Pat [Cummins] and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain.
